response: Yes, ultrasound can be a useful tool in the diagnosis and follow-up of constipated children. It is a non-invasive, pain-free, and radiation-free imaging modality that can help assess the severity of constipation, detect any underlying anatomical abnormalities, and monitor the effectiveness of treatment. Ultrasound can measure the thickness of the rectal wall, the diameter of the rectum, and the presence of feces in the rectum, which can help diagnose constipation and guide management. Additionally, ultrasound can be used to assess for any complications of constipation, such as rectal prolapse or fecal impaction. Overall, ultrasound is a valuable diagnostic tool in the evaluation and management of constipated children.
